title: Today / Morning Brief
markdown:
**What it is:** A single screen of *what needs you right now* — the proactive digest the Executive prepares so you're not the one chasing status. In the app it's the **Briefing**, the screen the app opens on.

**What it does:**

- Splits items into **Needs you** (waiting on your call) and **Across the team** (everything else in motion).
- Shows each department's goal health — on-track, at-risk, or off-track — with the at-risk goals called out.
- Lists people with open items, their reply counts, SLA status, and whether they're on leave.
- If your latest morning brief, end-of-day digest or weekly review couldn't be sent to you, a line at the top says why and what to connect. It goes away once that's fixed.
- Surfaces proposals and alerts you can click to open a chat thread with full context.

**How to use:**

1. Click **Briefing** in the sidebar (or the Open Executive logo).
2. Work the **Needs you** lane from the top, starting with the **Start here** card. Each card offers:
   - **✓ Approve** — accept the recommendation; a chat opens so the Executive can carry it out.
   - **✎ Edit & approve** — reword the action first, then **✓ Send approval**; your text is used exactly as written.
   - **💬 Discuss** (or click the card) — open a chat with the context already filled in.
   - **✕ Dismiss** — drop it and stay on the briefing.
   - **↪ Nudge *name*** — shown when the best move is chasing someone for a reply.
3. Some cards are simpler: a document card has one **✓ Mark reviewed** button, and a calendar-booking card books (or declines) the meeting directly when you click Approve or Dismiss.
4. Keep the lane tidy: **✕ Dismiss N older than 7 days** clears stale items, and **⟳ Re-check relevance** asks the Executive to review every open item now.
5. Click a department card to ask for that department's status in chat.

**Example:** in a Discuss thread, just say *"go ahead"* to approve the proposal or *"drop it"* to dismiss it — no need to go back to the card. (Calendar bookings still need the Approve button.)

**Just for yourself?** If you use Open Executive just for yourself (**Settings → Workspace → Just me**), the Briefing leaves out the team parts: there is no Departments or People card and no "Across the team" lane — everything that needs a decision is in **Needs you**. A **goals at risk** badge at the top opens **Goals** when one is slipping. Instead, **Your projects** lists the projects the Executive is tracking for you. Click **✓ Done** when one is finished, or **Drop** to stop tracking it (it asks first, and removes the project from Pulse). **Due soon** lists what you've promised by a date and what others have asked of you, due in the next week — say *"I'll send Northwind the proposal by Friday"* in the web chat or your own Slack or Discord and it shows up here, and the Executive reminds you when it's due. Click **✓ Done** once it's handled; **All open items** opens the full list. **Top three today** shows the three things to focus on today — the same three your morning brief opens with — each with a free slot in today's working hours when the Executive can read your calendar. **This week's review** shows your latest weekly review: when it ran and next week's top three. Click **Read the review** to see all of it.

Your morning brief also opens with a **top three for today**, picked from what's overdue or due, goals that are slipping and the projects you're driving. When Google Workspace is connected and the Executive can read your calendar (it is your own account, or you shared your calendar with it), each of the three gets a free slot in today's working hours and the brief lists today's meetings; otherwise the three come without times. Every Friday afternoon (in your time zone) a **weekly review** arrives the same way: your goals graded by area, what's due or overdue, projects that went quiet, the week's decisions, a few older decisions to look back on, and next week's top three. Both also show up on the Briefing (see above), so you see them even when no chat app or email is connected. When it asks how an older decision turned out, just tell the Executive in the web chat or your own Slack or Discord and it records the outcome against that decision.

*Note: proposals are routed to the right person automatically based on who has authority over them.*
